name: Kyoto
blurb: Online conversation regarding Kyoto reflects a declining trend (-51% versus baseline), with visitors discussing transit times, fine dining, and temple visits. Commuting between Osaka and Kyoto or navigating local bus congestion remains a frequently cited pain point.

positive: Praise for fine dining spots like Tokuha Motonari
Enjoyment of early morning visits to temples and gardens
Appreciation for scenic rooftop views and autumn weather
negative: Long, tiring daily commutes between Osaka and Kyoto
Crowded and slow local bus transit within the city
Frustration with heavy tourist crowds during peak times

quotes.text:
Part of the biggest problem is the commute: I work in Kyoto but live in Osaka, so that means 1.5 hours there and 1.5 hours back. 

An entire 3 hours of my day in transit. 

I have tried to work on the train (even writing fiction for myself!), but I’m just too tired

Set inside a remodeled sukiya house in residential Kuramaguchi, Tokuha Motonari has had one of the most rapid ascents to stardom within the recent Japanese fine dining scene. Once you …

To elaborate on my "almost never use Kyoto buses" point here…

For anyone who is not on a hostel-level budget while travelling, your time is more valuable than Kyoto buses.

The buses are so slow, crowded and uncomfortable that it's almost always worth doing train/subway + taxi instead.

One of the biggest #JohnDoesJapan gifts you can give yourself in Kyoto is to start at dawn:

• enjoy neighbourhoods and outdoor spaces like these before the crowds

• arrive at Big Name Temples a good 20-30 minutes before they open so you're in before the tour buses

• have a nice nap after lunch
